For Respondent-2 : Mr.R.Sivakumar  ORDER The Writ Petition is filed seeking declaration that the land acquisition proceedings initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in respect of 3 acres and 5227 sq.ft in S.NO.544/13 situate in Chettinaikenpatti Village, Dindigul District as lapsed in view of non payment of compensation as required under Section 24(2) or the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013(Act 30 of 2013).

sentences.text: 2.There is no representation on behalf of the Petitioner.
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the respondents and perused the materials placed before this Court.
3.In the affidavit filed in support of the Writ Petition, it is clearly admitted by the Petitioner that physical possession of the property has been taken by the respondents.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

4.As per the law laid down by the Apex Court in Indoor Development Authority .vs. Manoharlal and others repoted in AIR 2020 SC 1496 = MANU/SC/0300/2020, in order to invoke Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation Act and declare the lapse of acquisition proceedings under Section 24(2),the following two conditions shall be stisfied namely, (1) physical possession should not have been taken from the land owner and (2) the compensaion amount should not have been tendered to the land owner.

sentences.text:
The relevant discussion of Apex Court in the case cited supra reads as follows:
363.In view of the aforesaid discussion

, we answer the questions as under:
1.......
2.......
3.The word or used in Section 24(2) between possession and compensation hs to be read as nor or as and.

The deemed lapse of land acquisition proceddings under section 24(2) of the Act of 2013 takes place where due to inaction of authorities for five years or more prior to commencement of the said Act, the possession of land has not been taken nor compensation has been paid.
In other words, in case possession has been taken, compenation has not been paid, then the is no lapse.
Similarly, if compensation has been paid, possession has not been taken, then there is no lapse.
